messages.text:
View this post on the web at https://www.californiacurrent.org/p/prop-3-the-forever-tax
The Boy Who Cried “Temporary!”
Prop 3 is not a new school-funding measure. It is the final act in a long confidence game, a tax that began life as temporary, was later extended, and now seeks permanence under the soft lighting of “children’s education and health care.” It is a classic fable of institutional self-interest dressed in the language of compassion. Every California public school should teach this story as a warning.
None will.
Without the ignorant and gullible public, it wouldn’t work.
In 2012, voters approved Proposition 30, marketed as “Temporary Taxes to Fund Education.” The first word was the tell. Governor Jerry Brown and the California Teachers Association (CTA) sold it as a short-term bridge across a $6 billion recession shortfall. High earners would pay a bit more; the sales tax would rise a quarter-cent; the money would “protect” California classrooms. It passed with 55 percent of the vote.
“Temporary,” they said. “Trust us,” they said.
Four years later the CTA returned with Prop 55. This same coalition that had educated much of the electorate now asked that electorate to extend the income-tax rates through 2030. Proposition 55 passed with 63 percent. The “temporary” measure easily becomes a medium-term one.
The pattern was set: declare “crisis,” extract money, declare new crisis, extract again.
Now Comes Proposition 3
It’s billed as the California Children’s Education and Health Care Protection Act. Its purpose is simple: remove the expiration date on Prop 30. What began as temporary and was then prolonged would, under the new Prop 3, become permanent.
Shakespeare understood this move.
In Macbeth he warned us of those who  “Look like the innocent flower, but be the serpent under’t.”  Prop 3 is that flower covered serpent:  wrapped in the soft language of children’s education and health care, while delivering a permanent tax increase that serves the adults who administer it, not the students in whose name it is advanced.
The numbers are enormous. One True Passion?
The search for your one true passion is a game you win only by refusing to play. Dan Kennedy has spent a lifetime falling hard for callings that never called back, a fleeting fascination with airport freight work, songwriting despite no musical ability, van-life fantasies, and pandemic manuscripts his agent rejected. On pins and needles waiting for Room Service (November 13-16, 2026)?
Good news: the first round of tickets and rooms goes on sale Sunday, August 16, 2026, at 4pm PT. Only half of the tickets and rooms will be available at that time. The second sale will happen in early October.
Everything is more expensive than it used to be, and producing events is no exception. Both hotels hiked our prices this year, so most rooms went up by $20-$40 per night. However, we kept the total price the same for Art Rooms in the main hotel — it just didn’t feel right to ask those of you who are making art in those rooms to pay more.
Note: base pricing this year includes the cost of fees that were previously tacked on during checkout. The total prices aren’t too far off of last year’s, just without as many surprise fees at checkout.
Tickets will be priced on a sliding scale from $470.35-$720.63, including taxes and fees, which breaks down to a base price of $440-$675. Our break-even is approximately $560 per ticket, before fees and taxes. Anything higher helps us pay staff closer to living wages (the vast majority currently work for less) and increase our art budget (many artists partially or fully self-fund their projects). Here are some guidelines for considering what to contribute:
* Base price of $440-$500: If attending the event is already a stretch for you financially, or you struggle to meet your basic needs (also consider our Volunteer & Financial Aid programs; more info coming soon)
* Base price of $500-$575: If you’re able to financially meet your basic needs and have some expendable income for new items or occasional travel
* Base price of $575-$675: If you have considerable expendable income, savings, or access to familial wealth; work in tech; own a home, land, or other high-value assets; and/or have high earning power* (even if you aren’t using it)
Be mindful of the sliding scale when purchasing your ticket! We will not issue refunds for tickets accidentally purchased at unintended prices.
We expect tickets to sell out quickly. Queue up for the sale up to 20 minutes in advance by using your personal invitation link below. You do not have to madly refresh at exactly 3:40pm — the queue order will be randomized at 4pm. People arriving after 4pm will go to the back of the queue.

We've updated Lovable's Privacy Policy to make it clearer, reflect new Lovable
features and the laws where you live, and explain your choices in more detail.
The updated policy takes effect on September 9, 2026, and applies to your use of
Lovable from that date.
On a Business or Enterprise plan? This notice is intended for users on Free and
Pro plans. If you've received it and your workspace is on a Business or
Enterprise plan, these changes do not modify your agreement with Lovable. Your
organization's data continues to be handled under your Data Processing Agreement
and contract terms, which this update does not change. Questions:
privacy@lovable.dev [privacy@lovable.dev].

the effective date, we may use Customer Content — your prompts (including images
and files you attach), code, project files, and generated outputs — and usage
data from Free and Pro plans to train, develop, and improve our AI models. You
can opt out at any time in Account Settings → Privacy. Opt out before the
effective date and your data is not used for training at all; opt out later and
your data is excluded going forward.
Importantly: We will not use your apps' end-user data or your account and
billing details for training.

described in the policy at any time.
Thanks for building with Lovable,

Volume 30, Issue #30 | August 7, 2026
Our community respects the environment. We are committed to leaving no physical trace of our activities wherever we gather. We clean up after ourselves and endeavor, whenever possible, to leave such places in a better state than when we found them.
- Leaving No Trace principle, written by Burning Man's Founder Larry Harvey in 2004
Burning Man has long been a laboratory for sustainability innovation; four decades of Communal Effort in Black Rock City and beyond has had a powerful impact on events and communities around the world.
And the innovation continues! In 2025, Burning Man Project operations  reduced fossil fuel emissions by 48% [https://journal.burningman.org/2026/07/black-rock-city/leaving-no-trace/the-race-to-decarbonize-black-rock-city/]. Across the city as a whole, fossil fuel emissions were at least 25% lower than they would have been without solar, batteries, and renewable fuels. If you’re involved with a Regional Event, be sure to check out the  Green Regionals Grant [https://burningman.org/arts-innovation/sustainability/green-regionals-grant/], a $30,000 grant for projects that help Regional Events and 10 Principled gatherings become more sustainable, regenerative, and resilient.
If you're headed to the dust this year, listen up! Everyone in Black Rock City has a role in minimizing the collective ecological impact on the Black Rock Desert, and on the Earth. There is no trash collection in Black Rock City. All your trash must leave with you. Remove all excess packaging from your stuff before you hit the road. Secure the load on your vehicle so nothing blows away. Better yet, reduce carbon emissions by  taking the Burner Express Bus [https://burnerexpress.burningman.org/burner-express-bus-tickets/] to the dust. On your way home, please only drop off trash and recycling at one of these  Burner-friendly disposal sites [https://survival.burningman.org/leave-no-trace/leave-nevada-beautiful/].

Today’s post is brought to you by my sponsor, Mechanize [ https://substack.com/redirect/77e10a65-e826-47ba-aff7-3945a1a93fd7?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ]. They’re hiring junior software engineers [ https://substack.com/redirect/07a28b6c-ad90-464a-b3ce-9b7417d68d01?j=eyJ1IjoiN2EzYzFhIn0.gmSjAtdlofMqOFUjgfQgnPyMBlCD_j00mTQEinip6mM ] at $300K/year base salary.
I often see people suggesting that there are countries that are richer than the U.S. This is true if we include wealthy micronations like Monaco or Liechtenstein; it is not true if we look at ‘real’ countries. This fact is sometimes obscured, however, by problematically inflated GDP figures for ‘real’ countries that are tax havens—such as Singapore, Switzerland, and Ireland—, and countries with extraordinary levels of inequality—like Qatar or the United Arab Emirates. But we can overcome these issues.
First, we have to figure out what to measure. The answer is not GDP per capita. Let’s ascend the ladder of comparisons!
GDP Per Capita: This is our familiar starting point.
GDP Per Capita, PPP: This is GDP per capita, but it also adjusts for price levels between countries. The adjustment is required because a dollar buys a different amount in different places. For America, rungs 1 and 2 are the same.
Net National Income Per Capita: This is like GDP Per Capita PPP, but it adjusts to account for the reality that capital wears out and some income belongs to foreigners.
Final Consumption Per Capita: This is actually what people consume, which is what their quality of life is based on in the immediate term. This penalizes thrifting.
Actual Individual Consumption: This is like final consumption per capita, except it accounts for the fact that some consumption is done collectively, and it uses consumption prices to promote comparability, too. This also counts out the things that we cannot attribute identifiably to people, like spending on defense and police, and it makes stuff like a publicly- and privately-funded hip replacement both get counted similarly, as the same sort of consumption.
And here’s where things get debatable:
Median AIC: A mean is not a typical person; rather, it’s distorted by outliers.
Low-Percentile AIC: A median is not a poor person, whose lives we’re interested in.

View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/e382b926e49e/thank-you-for-your-interest-in-humanmades-hardware-accelerator-12854328?e=586e46fdfc)
** Join us for a mixer discussion about preparing hardware for manufacturing and production!
------------------------------------------------------------
Preparing hardware for manufacturing and production.
​A prototype proves that an idea can work. Building a product that can be manufactured reliably, affordably, and at scale is a very different challenge.
​This Founder Session explores what it takes to bridge that gap. Through real-world experience and practical discussion, our speakers will share lessons from bringing hardware products into production, navigating manufacturing decisions, and avoiding common pitfalls that can slow down—or derail—the journey from prototype to product.
​Joining us will be Steve Dussé. He has a decades-long track record of bringing products from back-of-the napkin sketches to high volume, low cost manufacturing spanning consumer electronics, IOT devices and power products.  EE by training, Steve has led product development across a variety of engineering disciplines.  Steve is currently VP Engineering for SPAN.IO (http://span.io/?utm_source=luma) overseeing a portfolio of smart circuit breaker panels
Whether you’re still refining your first prototype or beginning conversations with manufacturers, you’ll leave with a better understanding of what production readiness really looks like.
​Topics may include:
* ​Designing for manufacturing and repeatability
* ​Choosing manufacturing processes and production pathways
* ​Working with suppliers and manufacturing partners
* ​Understanding cost, quality, and scalability tradeoffs
* ​Common production challenges—and how to avoid them
* ​Audience Q&A
Whether you’re building your first hardware product or simply curious about what it takes to manufacture one, you’re welcome to join us.
Doors open at 4:30 PM for networking with founders, builders, and members of the Humanmade community. Presentations begin at 5:00 PM, followed by additional time to connect and continue the conversation until 7:00 PM.
​Space is limited. RSVP required.
